paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy of various editing methods across different co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale, featuring visible tick labels at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$ without specified units. Data points along the x-axis are positioned at approximate values of 3, 30, 300, and 3000. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" to denote percentage, using a linear scale with tick marks at regular intervals of 5, ranging from 40 to 65. Six distinct solid lines represent the different methods evaluated. The "Base" method, shown by a black line with circle markers, starts at approximately 38 at the lowest x-value, increases to roughly 44 at an x-value of 300, and remains nearly flat to end at 44. The "FT" method is a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers that exhibits a steady upward trend from an initial value of 40 to a final value of approximately 48. The "IKE" method, represented by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starts near 43 and gradually increases to end at roughly 49.5. The "MEND" method is depicted by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at about 44.5, rising to 54 at an x-value of 300, and ending at 56.5. The "MEMIT" method, shown as a purple line with pentagon markers, begins at approximately 43.5, increases to 51 at an x-value of 30, and then rises more gradually to finish at roughly 54.5. Finally, the "ROME" method is represented by a green line with square markers; it starts at approximately 51 and increases consistently across the x-axis to reach the highest final value of 66.
